7. [RLOW.14.7] **A synthesized terminal takes the position of the
   rule that induced it.** Some terminals have no rule of their own in
   source: the follow-up rule an `after` clause lowers to ([LTAC.3.1]),
   the sibling rules a `call` continuation lowers to ([LCCO.10.1]), and the
   `_answered` and `_failed` rules each `timeout` clause lowers to
   ([LCCO.7.6]). The compiler must emit each such terminal **after the
   terminal of the rule that induced it, and before any later author
   rule's**, in this order:

   - the inducing rule's own terminal;
   - then the follow-up of each of its `after` clauses, in source order;
   - then the sibling of each of its `call` continuations, in source
     order. A `timeout` clause's sibling is followed, after every terminal
     it induces, by that clause's `_answered` rule and then its `_failed`
     rule, and only then by the next continuation's sibling.

   The order applies at every level. Each synthesized terminal is
   followed at once by the terminals it induces in turn, a nested
   `after`'s follow-up ([LTAC.6.2.2]) or the sibling of a continuation in
   its body, ordered the same way, and only then by the next terminal at
   its own level.

   So the emitted sequence is a depth-first walk: each author rule, then
   everything it induced, then the next author rule. A synthesized terminal's ordinal is therefore determined
   by the source that induced it, exactly as an author rule's is, and
   [RLOW.14.3]'s "canonical source order" is total over every terminal
   rather than only over the ones a reader can point at.
